companyIntro.name: Pixel & Pine Studio
companyIntro.mission: Design digital products that real people can actually use on the first try.
companyIntro.culture: Test with users early and often. Opinions are hypotheses until a user confirms them.

projectBackground.name: Checkout Flow Optimisation
projectBackground.context: Customers abandon at the payment step. The team has opinions; you have a prototype and five participants.

manager.name: Inês Carvalho
manager.note: Don't tell me what you like. Tell me what users did.

assignment.title: Find and fix the checkout problems
assignment.brief: Plan the test, calculate success rate, apply heuristics and write the findings.

documents.name: Checkout Prototype
documents.note: Error messages appear only in red text; no progress indicator.

tasks.title: Sample Size
tasks.prompt: Why are five participants often enough for a first usability round?
options: They typically reveal most major issues; run more rounds after fixes
tasks.reasoning: Small iterative tests find most problems cheaply.
tasks.mistake: One large late test finds problems too late.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Task Success Rate
tasks.prompt: 14 of 20 task attempts succeeded. What is the success rate?
tasks.reasoning: Success rate is a core usability metric.
tasks.mistake: Counting participants instead of attempts changes the result.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Heuristic
tasks.prompt: The user can't tell whether the order is processing. Which heuristic is violated?
tasks.reasoning: Users need feedback about what the system is doing.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Form Problems
tasks.prompt: Select issues that hurt the form.
options: Errors shown only in red without text
tasks.reasoning: Colour-only errors and hidden progress hurt accessibility and confidence.
tasks.mistake: Relying on colour excludes colour-blind users.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Card Sorting
tasks.prompt: When is card sorting most useful?
options: To understand how users group content for navigation
tasks.reasoning: It reveals mental models for information architecture.
tasks.mistake: Designing navigation from internal structure confuses users.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Findings Summary
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence summary of the findings and recommended changes.
tasks.modelAnswer: Seventy percent of checkout attempts succeeded, and failures clustered on the payment step where errors appeared only in red and there was no progress indicator. This matches the 42% analytics drop-off. We recommend adding clear error text, a progress indicator and visible confirmation after payment. We should retest with five new participants after the changes and track drop-off for two weeks.
tasks.reasoning: A good summary links qualitative and quantitative evidence and proposes testable changes.
tasks.mistake: Opinions without evidence won't convince stakeholders.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: Beautiful and Unusable
caseStudy.background: A redesigned app won a design award yet conversion fell 18%. Users couldn't find the checkout button hidden in a hamburger menu.
caseStudy.challenges: Design was reviewed by peers, not tested with users.
questions: What test would have caught it?
How do you balance aesthetics and clarity?
caseStudy.solution: Pixel & Pine added a five-user test before every release.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Test with users early; beauty isn't usability.

prompts: How do you separate your taste from user needs?
